Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:3499` ⇒ **`domain:services`** (plugin-auth joined that lane in the 2026-08-19 merge). Type **Bug** — confirmed as filed. **`pm:queue`**, dispatchable now: named line, captured stack, proposed fix shape, and a pin design, all from a real composed boot.

⭐ **The reason no suite caught it is the most useful thing on the card, and it should shape the pin rather than just explain the past.** `(logger?.error ?? logger?.warn)?.(…)` **detaches** the method before calling, so it runs with `this === undefined`. A plain-closure logger — which is what nearly every test double is — survives that; `@objectstack/core`'s class-based logger dereferences `this.writeErrorLike` and throws. ⇒ The bug is invisible to any double that is a bare function. **The regression pin must use a class-based logger double whose methods actually read `this`**; a closure double will pass against the broken code and pin nothing.

**Not a security defect, stated so it is not mis-escalated**: the gate still refuses — the refusal is simply reported as a 500 with the verdict swallowed instead of the 4xx that names it. It fails **closed**. ⛔ No `security` label, and it is not on the permission manual floor. The cost is diagnostic: the operator gets `500 null` and debugs blind while the real message ("the declared self-registration permission set … cannot be resolved") never reaches either the caller or the log.

**No `target:v17`, and the contrast with #12772 is the reason** — that card is graded a release blocker this same round, and this one is not. This defect lives on an **error path**: it degrades the report of a refusal that is already happening, on a deployment that is already misconfigured. Real, worth fixing quickly, but it does not break a working install. ⛔ Not a gradient judgement — the four blocking classes take a deployment that works today and stop it, and this does not.

**Scope — the sweep is in scope to *enumerate*, ⛔ not to fix repo-wide:**

- ✅ Fix the named site, keeping both the fallback and the receiver (`logger?.error ? logger.error(message, meta) : logger?.warn?.(message, meta)`, or `.call(logger, …)`), plus the class-based-logger pin.
- ✅ Run the card's suggested grep for `(logger?.error ?? logger?.warn)` and sibling detach-then-call shapes, and **report the full list** — the card is right that this probably has family.
- ✅ Fix any siblings **inside `plugin-auth`** in the same PR: same package, same shape, same pin covers them.
- ⛔ Siblings in **other packages** go on a follow-up card, not this PR. They are other lanes' files, and a repo-wide receiver-detachment sweep is its own reviewable unit — folding it in here would turn a one-line fix into a cross-lane diff nobody can review against a single defect.

If the grep comes back with a large family in one other package, say so in the report and this seat will decide fold-or-serial on the enumeration rather than on a guess.

Dedup: no existing card on receiver-detached logger calls in this repo.

## Claim + dispatch — and the enumeration triage asked for is already in hand

- **Session**: `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5` (`os-litant`, `domain:services` execution seat)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-12773-logger-receiver-detach`
- **Worktree**: `../objectstack-12773` (per-repo; ⛔ never the shared checkout; ⛔ never `git stash`)
- **Model**: `claude-opus-5` — clause-② `no` (see below)
- `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`

## ⭐ Answering triage's fold-or-serial question before the dev runs

Triage wrote: *"If the grep comes back with a large family in one other package, say so in the report and this seat will decide fold-or-serial on the enumeration rather than on a guess."*

**It does, and here is the enumeration — measured on `origin/main` at `ead731756`, so the decision can be made on facts rather than after a round trip:**

- **`plugin-auth`: exactly 1 site** — the named one, now at `auth-manager.ts:3610` (⚠️ the card says `:3499`; main has moved and the line drifted, so re-locate rather than trusting either number).
- **`driver-sql`: 10 sites**, one file (`sql-driver.ts`), spelling `(this.logger.error ?? this.logger.warn)(…)` / `(this.logger.info ?? this.logger.warn)(…)` — among them `:10575`, `:10744`, `:10791`, `:11408`, `:11415`, `:11426`.
- Nothing else found by that shape.

⇒ **Serial, not folded** — which is what triage's own fence already prescribed, and the enumeration confirms rather than contradicts it. Filed as **#12792**, unassigned and ungraded.

⭐ Two things make #12792 stronger than a bare grep hit, and they are why it is worth a card rather than a footnote:

1. **The same file already contains the correct spelling.** `sql-driver.ts:4320`, `logDurabilityFailure`, is `if (this.logger.error) this.logger.error(msg, meta); else this.logger.warn(msg, meta)` — a property-access call, receiver bound. The fix shape exists three lines long in the same class as the 10 sites that do not use it.
2. **A careful docblock at `:4290` explicitly left those 10 alone — on a different axis.** It is about `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` being unable to see a call on a parenthesized expression, and closes *"left alone on purpose — they are a separate change with a separate blast radius."* The **receiver** question was never in its scope. Two orthogonal problems share one syntax; one was reasoned about with care and the other rode along invisibly.

⚠️ ⛔ **Not established, and #12792 says so**: whether those 10 actually crash. That needs a receiver-sensitive logger, and I have not measured what `SqlDriver` is handed in any real composition. ⛔ **This dispatch does not touch driver-sql.**

## Scope for this PR — triage's, unchanged

- ✅ Fix `auth-manager.ts:3610`, keeping **both** the fallback and the receiver.
- ✅ ⭐ **The pin must use a class-based logger double whose methods actually read `this`.** This is the single most important line in triage's grading: a bare-closure double **passes against the broken code and pins nothing**. If your double is a plain function, you have written a test that cannot fail.
- ✅ Report the sweep. Mine above is a starting point, ⛔ not a substitute — re-derive it, and **broaden past my regex**: I searched syntactic `(a ?? b)(…)` shapes only, so a `const fn = logger.error; fn(…)` detachment would **not** have been found and was not searched for. Say what you covered.
- ✅ Fix siblings **inside `plugin-auth`** in the same PR if the broader sweep finds any (mine found none beyond the named site).
- ⛔ Siblings in other packages ⇒ **#12792**, not this PR.

## Grading notes carried from triage, so they are not re-derived

⛔ **No `security` label and not the permission manual floor** — the gate still refuses; it fails **closed**. The cost is diagnostic: `500 null` instead of the 4xx that names the verdict. ⛔ **No `target:v17`** — this degrades the report of a refusal on an already-misconfigured deployment; it does not take a working install and stop it.

**Clause ② — `no`.** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read live at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:3813` this pass: `claude-fable-5`, not applicable. The declared refusal is unchanged; a crash stops pre-empting it. ⚠️ Falsifiable — re-derive the gate union live on your actual changed set, and if it names a **contract** family, ⛔ stop and report.

## Fences

⛔ Never `content/docs/releases/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. ⛔ **Draft PR only** — this seat lands it. Changeset required.

⛔ **Never accept `pnpm --filter X run <script>` as a measurement without first confirming `X` declares that script** — a package lacking it matches nothing, runs nothing and **exits 0**. ⚠️ `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is **NOT MEASURED**, never a pass or a fail. Any zero-hit needs a **positive control first**.

⭐ **Prove the pin can go red**: revert the fix under the new test and watch exactly it fail; confirm the mutation on disk by `git hash-object` rather than an editor exit code; restore with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` (⛔ never bare) and verify by hash equality plus an empty `git status --porcelain`.

## PM review of record — **ACCEPT**. The sweep found two sites my instrument was blind to, and the blind spot was the exact one I flagged.

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. PR #12803. ⛔ Not armed — CI started 21:09Z, most jobs `in_progress`; entry qualification is **every** check green.

## ⭐ The family inside `plugin-auth` is 3, not 1 — and I handed over a count that said 1

My dispatch enumeration said *"`plugin-auth`: exactly 1 site"*, with the caveat that I had searched syntactic `(a ?? b)(…)` only and that a `const fn = logger.error; fn(…)` detachment *"would NOT have been found and was not searched for."* The dev broadened to exactly that form and found **two more live sites**, both verified here independently on `origin/main`:

```
reconcile-membership.ts:161   const log = deps.logger?.error ?? deps.logger?.warn;
                        :162  log?.(message, { …meta, policy: described, expected: MEMBERSHIP_POLICIES });

adopt-membership.ts:239       const log = options.logger?.info ?? ((msg, meta) => console.info(msg, meta));
                        :240  log( …
```

Both are in scope per triage (*"fix any siblings inside `plugin-auth` in the same PR"*) and both are fixed. ⚠️ The second is the subtler one — its *fallback* is a bound closure, so it only crashes when `options.logger?.info` exists, which is precisely the real-composition case.

⇒ The caveat I attached was not decoration: it was load-bearing, and honouring it doubled the defect count in this package.

## The receiver question is now measured, not assumed

The dev read `packages/core/src/logger.ts` and reported that **every** `ObjectLogger` channel dereferences `this` with no constructor binding. Verified here: the four channels are declared as methods at `:401` (`debug`), `:405` (`info`), `:409` (`warn`), `:413` (`error`), with **9** `this.write` / `this.writeErrorLike` dereferences among them.

⇒ All three sites crash against the platform's own logger — ⛔ not just the one the card named from a single dogfood boot.

## ⭐ And it found the mechanism behind `500 null`, which the card described but did not explain

`audienceLogError` is called at `auth-manager.ts:3724` **inside a `try` whose `catch` at `:3735` calls the same helper again** — so the logging failure throws, the catch tries to log the failure with the same broken helper, and the second throw escapes the gate entirely. That is why a refusal became a bodyless 500 rather than a stray error line next to a correct 4xx. Nobody asked for this and it is the difference between "the log is missing" and "the verdict is destroyed".

## Instrument discipline — two of its own regexes were wrong, and it said so

- The `(a ?? b)(…)` pattern **initially matched nothing — including the known defect site.** Caught by the absence of the positive control, not by luck.
- The assignment-detachment pattern was anchored at `^`, so it missed **every indented `const`** — which is every real site. ⭐ **Fixing that anchor is what surfaced both extra siblings.**

Both were repaired before use and reported rather than quietly re-run. Every zero-hit claim carries a validated positive control behind it.

**Ablation: three legs, one per fixed site**, each mutating back to the detached form and running the **whole** package suite so *"and no others failed"* is measured across all 1695 tests rather than asserted. Exact failure counts (2 / 2 / 1), each failing with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` — structurally identical to the production `reading 'writeErrorLike'`. The replacement asserted an **exact hit count of 1 and aborted otherwise**, so the zero-hit no-op that bit another dev in this lane today could not have reported green here.

## ⛔ Correcting my own filed card

The dev measured **9** call sites in `driver-sql`, where my dispatch brief and **#12792 itself** said 10. It is right and I was wrong: my `grep -c` counts matching **lines**, and `sql-driver.ts`'s docblock **quotes the pattern in prose** while explaining why the named method exists. I counted that prose as a call site — the exact error (*"`grep -F` matches inside comments; read the matched line"*) I have been holding others to all shift. #12792 is corrected with the complete 9-site list.

## Two non-filings, both correctly judged

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts:1033` and `dev-restart.ts:275`** — same shape, outside the fence, ⛔ left alone. And **not filed**, because `dev-restart`'s fallback is `console.log`, which is bound in Node ⇒ ⭐ it declined to file a card on a shape it had not shown to crash. That is the right bar.
- **`plugin-auth`'s tsconfig excluding `**/*.test.ts`** — not filed, because it is a *declared, ratcheted* `TEST_DEBT` entry already governed by #6376, not an undeclared gap. It measured 94 errors with the diff and 94 with the sources reverted, so the ledger drift is entirely pre-existing and none of it is this PR's.
